topic: B2B SEO in the Age of AI Search
headline: AI’s Impact Is Outrunning Measurement: The Trust And Attribution Gap Facing Brands via @sejournal, @gregjarboe
keyNotes: The biggest challenge with new AI tools is that their impact is growing so fast, we can't properly measure if they're actually helping businesses or not. This means companies are spending money on AI without truly knowing the return on their investment, like Meta burning through 73.7 trillion "tokens" (a unit of data processed by AI) without a clear benefit.

Even if an AI tool suggests something as the top answer, people will often choose a brand they already know and trust, even if it's lower down the list. This shows that building a good reputation is becoming even more important than just being the first result, with roughly three out of four consumers preferring a trusted name.

Many companies publicly blamed AI for job cuts, but it turns out these layoffs were often due to other reasons like hiring too many people during the pandemic or not managing money well. AI was just a convenient excuse, with over 87,000 job cuts attributed to AI through May, but often for reasons unrelated to AI's operational reality.

The old ways we used to measure how well our online content was doing, especially with search engines, don't work anymore for AI-powered search. For example, Google's own data is reportedly 75% incomplete for this new kind of search, meaning businesses are largely flying blind when trying to understand their online presence.
question: The article points out that the old ways we measure success online, like tracking simple search rankings, are now "75% incomplete" for understanding how AI impacts businesses. If you were to look at your own work or industry, what "old scoreboards" might you still be using that are no longer accurately reflecting the real impact of new technologies or changing customer behaviors?
